# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document accompanies
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md) and
> expands the RFC’s phase sequence into **independently committable and independently verifiable**
> three-level tasks.
>
> The phase order and acceptance gates are governed solely by the main body of RFC-039. This
> document is responsible only for decomposing the work into an executable granularity and recording
> conflicts whose resolution is still pending.

**Reserved numbers (not reclaimed)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`. None of the three
has had a corresponding entry since the WBS was established—the entire history of this document has
zero matches for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1`
(`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md` can be used to verify this),
and there are no repository-wide references either. `8.1` corresponds precisely to phase 1 of `05`
(test revival and completion). That phase was split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so P8’s
numbering is aligned with its phase numbers (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so on).

**Covered by this document**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and binding
of acceptance criteria.

**Not covered by this document**: the design rationale for tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the rationale
for phase ordering (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: newly registered Level 2/Level 3 entries **must
contain two fields**—“**Owning phase**” (the P to which the entry truly belongs, which may differ
from the containing section) and “**Blocks the main line**”; `awaiting scheduling` is no longer the
default state, and an unmarked entry is considered **not schedulable**. Numbers **must be unique
throughout the document** (cross-track tasks use their track number, such as `029g.x`, and must not
occupy `N.x`). **Check-off/completion records are based on “task id + evidence (gate value, run id,
issue number, file:line)” and do not record commit hashes**—`pull --rebase` rewrites local hashes,
so hard-coded hashes inevitably become invalid (2026-10-13 example: `94ad03ce4`→`631eb3e3c`). Use
`git log` to find commit hashes.

## Current State: Gaps Discovered During Decomposition

When the “Implementation Points” from eight documents were consolidated into the main table, **five
hard gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been resolved:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Resolution                                                                                                                                                           |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps**. RFC-039 defines P5 (splitting the checker) and its acceptance criteria (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents describes how that split should be performed; the directory tree in `01-routing.md` contains an `annotations.rs` entry, the only mention in the entire batch.                                              | P5’s steps are supplied by this document (see below).                                                                                                                |
| G2  | **Three ownership claims for the `include!` refactor, with no implementation anywhere**. RFC-039 lists it under P4; `02` assigns the reference to itself; S7 in `06` also lists it. However, the modification list in `02` (6 additions + 20 modifications) **does not contain `semantic_tokens.rs`**.                                                                | The implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 of this document (prerequisite: P4 complete); the references in RFC-039 and `06` have been updated to point here.   |
| G3  | **Three concurrent CI-script inventories**. `RFC` lists four `scripts/ci/*.py`; `01` lists four scripts + one `cargo test`; `07` lists four differently named checks; `04` additionally requires `check-synth-boundary.py`. After deduplication, there are **at least nine new scripts and no unified inventory**; `check-obligations.py` is owned by both P4 and P9. | The unified inventory appears in §P9 of this document (11 scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents refer to this table.                                |
| G4  | **Conflict over the life cycle of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1005 lines that must be revived,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with the `Precedence` enum”; `05` advocates deletion.                                                                                                                         | **Revive in P1, delete with Pratt in P8** (decision recorded as C1)—first restore CI coverage, then perform the deletion in 8.6 alongside the dead ladder.           |
| G5  | **Conflict in the wording of the L2 goal**. RFC-039 and the index in this directory say “grammar-driven syntax,” but `05` self-assesses that it **“did not use true grammar-driven parsing (LALRPOP); it only achieved declarative table lookup.”**                                                                                                                   | This has converged on **complete LALRPOP grammar-driven parsing** (05 §Syntax: Complete Grammar-Driven Parsing); the G7/G8 acceptance gates enforce that commitment. |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0  仓库维护机制与代码放置规程     08        ← 新增，先立规矩
P1  复活孤儿测试并修缺陷           06 §S1
P2  建立等价性判据基线             07 全部
P3  修正确性漏洞（最小方案）        02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4  阶段契约与统一 Driver          02
P5  checker 文件内拆分             02 + 本文补齐
P6  类型表示单一化                 03
P7  中间表示 SSA 化                04      } 可并行
P8  前端范式变更                   05      }
P9  防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单）     01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正             06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: the three prohibitions (no invention, no endless padding, and no
patching when a refactor is required) constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be
established before work begins; otherwise, while reviving tests in P1, work would already be adding
`mod` declarations to `tests/mod.rs`—precisely the source of the G4 conflict.

      2026-10-24, issue [#501](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/501); source = F4
      tracing during round 2 of the 4.10 batch review: a **parenthesized function type** in return
      position is decomposed at the wrong level—`g: () -> ((x: Int) -> Int) = inc` reports E1012 and
      expects `int64` (the annotation is read as **curried**, meaning “one value parameter,
      returning Int”), while `g: () -> ((x: Int) -> Int) = () => { return inc }` expects
      `fn(int64)->int64` but finds the lambda’s **overall** type (`fn() -> fn(int64)->int64`); the
      two paths give **mutually contradictory expectations** for the same annotation, so a function
      “declaring a function-type return” **has no valid annotation form** (removing the annotation
      makes it pass). **The annotation itself parses correctly** (measured, ruling out the parser).
      **Owning phase: P3; Blocks the main line: No**)

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted on 2026-10-02,
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactoring itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by
the ordering constraint**; it is distinct from P10 S5 “reduce the visibility of `pub` items” (Rust’s
`pub(crate)` narrowing).

**Why the whole track must precede P4**: 029g’s deletion surface overlaps with the rewrite surface
of all four refactoring phases. Reversing the order means repeating the same deletions and baseline
updates on the new grammar / new checker layout / new SSA IR.

**Acceptance (behavioral changes, red criterion first)**:

1. **Red before green**: each of the two behavioral changes must land a red criterion before code
   changes—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② an unreferenced top-level
   binding in a Lib/Script role newly reports W1001 (pub items were previously absolutely exempt).
2. **Test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` cases in
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixtures, equivalent new cases must
   replace them.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (new parse errors + new W1001) ⇒ update
   the corpus differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG in the
   same commit; IR snapshots are expected to be zero-diff, and any non-zero difference requires an
   explanation.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` all green.

**Ordering**: overlaps with 3.4 files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must be serial and
cannot run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g track does not
depend on 3.4; the implementer chooses the order based on the work at hand.

> **Commit cross-reference (2026-10-08)**: the adoption of this section (the P3.5 chapter +
> main-chain/constraint row) was merged into `97071c81b` along with RFC-039’s D56 while a parallel
> flow was cleaning the workspace; the commit message records “3.4 addendum registration + D57/D58
> decision archiving” and does not mention this track. History is not rewritten; following the
> existing convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 landing note), it is recorded in place
> as a retrospective bisection reference.

| 5.2 Extract `refinement`    | 5.2.1 Move out the refinement blocks (three noncontiguous sections of the original `checker.rs`; now the single file `checker/refinement.rs`, containing `ReturnRefinement` / `RefinedWalkCtx`), leaving the retained surface and the six cross-boundary shared items in place                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | 5.1.1        | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|                             | 5.2.2 Refine the entry point to “`&self` + return diagnostics,” **without leaving the impl**: `collect_refined_binding_checks` (now `checker/refinement.rs`, `pub(super)`) no longer uses `&mut self` to write implicitly to the error channel; the diagnostic set is returned upward, and the sole write point is the sole caller `check_module_impl` (`checker.rs`, symbol location). **Reason for not leaving the impl**: the only field this family uses is `self.env` (so leaving the impl is technically feasible), but converting both the entry point and traversal to free functions would move these call sites: eight production call sites of `resolve_type_annotation` (six annotation paths + `refined_walk_stmt` + `collect_refined_var_names_in_stmt`), two production call sites + one test call site of `collect_param_refinements`, and would create a reverse dependency from the “retained surface (signature collection)” to refinement—the opposite of the coupling this step intends to eliminate | 5.2.1        | C1 zero-diff; four **symbol criteria**: ① the signature contains no `&mut self` ② the function body contains zero `env.errors` ③ the **returned** diagnostics have exactly one write point in the caller ④ the entry point still has one location |
| 5.3 Extract `annotations`   | 5.3.1 Move out the ten-item annotation-validation family (now the single file `checker/annotations.rs`; `check_annotation_type_names` is the `pub(super)` entry point, the other nine items are private to the family, and `is_predicate_head` is a free function within the family)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | 5.2.2        | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|                             | 5.3.2 **`collect_used_in_type` (`pub(crate)`) remains `pub(crate)` and remains under the `checker` module path**: it is a **shared-surface** function (consumed on both sides by `collect_function_signature` and `inference/statements.rs:16`), and 5.3.1 was empirically **not** migrated ⇒ the “zero caller changes” criterion **was already satisfied**, so **do not add** a new `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export. **Constraint retained**: if it is ever migrated with the family (into annotations or another later batch), `checker.rs` must add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that this import remains byte-for-byte unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | 5.3.1        | **Zero caller changes** is the hard acceptance criterion for this step: `git diff src/frontend/core/typecheck/inference/statements.rs` is empty                                                                                                   |

**Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is ever migrated with the annotation family, `checker.rs` **must then** add a
`pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the import remains unchanged; 5.3 did not migrate
it, so this batch added no re-export (the criterion was already satisfied).

**Split only proven large blocks.** Do not split modules that are only 200–400 lines long—that
increases navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and provides no decoupling benefit. The remaining
submodules (signatures / type_defs / imports) are to be split after their files grow back to 1,500
lines.

**Hard acceptance** (**criterion revised on 2026-10-27, following decision ② of 2026-10-26**):
`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be empty in **each round of
6.1–6.7**. **Direct-drive test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly drive modified code, such
as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be changed when mechanically required, but every change
must be registered with **file / line count / rationale**; **tests must not be deleted and
assertions must not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral-fix** batch (new
diagnostic code + baseline update), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion, and is
handled as a separate round with a separate decision.

> **Revision relationship**: the original criterion (decision ② of 2026-10-26) was written as
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, applying a blanket zero-difference requirement to all of
> `tests/`; the revised criterion **only changes direct-drive test files from “zero difference” to
> “may be changed but must register file / line count / rationale”**, while the zero-difference
> requirements for the corpus layer (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and
> standard library (`src/std/`) remain unchanged. First application = 6.1.2: only
> `tests/formatter_integration.rs` changed, by **3 lines** (two `assert_format_eq` expectations
> `i64`→`Int64` + one comment), with the rationale that the expected type name in the assertion must
> be synchronized with the changed spelling; no test was deleted and no assertion was weakened. See
> 09a “P6 6.1 Name Normalization Closure.”

### P9 Anti-Rebound Gates (Unified Script Inventory — This Document Supplements Original Gap G3)

Source: [01](01-routing.md) §Anti-Rebound Mechanism + [08](08-maintenance-mechanism.md)
§Machine-Checkable Rules

**This is the sole authoritative inventory of all CI scripts** (11 scripts). Scripts are integrated
into CI at their “introduction phase”; those marked report-only are converted to hard failures
uniformly in P9 (changing from “report” to “fail”). Existing violations (parallel representations,
disambiguation aliases, etc.) must wait until P6/P8 to reach zero; converting them to hard failures
early would leave CI permanently red and lead people to bypass the gates. When P9 hardens them, the
gates should be exactly green. P2’s 2.5, P4’s 4.3.2, and P7’s 7c.1 refer to this table and do not
define separate inventories.

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 hemorrhage-control path (decision of 2026-10-05)**: P3’s prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR
> verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential and performance baseline) can proceed in
> parallel with P3. Hemorrhage control for correctness defects is not blocked by criterion
> infrastructure; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified Driver requires all
> three layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every P1 action (1.2.x is precisely the act of adding `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                             |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Vulnerability criteria must be **written in red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3), and the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so the red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                   |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order would cause bugs to become fixed as “established behavior” in the stage table                                                                                                                                                                     |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g (#399)’s deletion surface covers the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 respectively (inventory in this document’s §P3.5)—reversing the order means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56)                                    |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` refactor and checker split modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated, or regressions cannot be bisected                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations are not converged first, the new IR will grow into a third representation; P7’s gate for the #529 implementation track is 6.9.1–6.9.4, while 6.9.5 does not block it, but P7 may consume only the quantifier-derived view and defeq interface, not build a parallel ledger |
| P7/P8 → P9                | The 9.5 snapshot baseline and the 9.3 `pub(crate)` leak count reach their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                              |

### Parallelization Groups

| Group                                    | Members                                                                               | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only group authorized by RFC)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                               | Disjoint file sets: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                         |
| B                                        | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                         | Each independently adds a `mod`; revert file by file                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| C                                        | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                       | The three criterion layers are independent                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| D                                        | 4.4 (proof-layer closure) ∥ the entire P6 line                                        | `02` explicitly states S5 “should proceed independently of S1–S4”                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| E                                        | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                                 | All depend only on 4.1 and are mutually independent                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| F                                        | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced under P0 can be developed in parallel) | The 9.5 snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| G                                        | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                          | Disjoint file sets (verified on 2026-10-05: S3 modifies `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 modifies `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 modifies two `pub` sites in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pair overlaps) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (same
batch of B6/E5 files); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (now unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (the same `checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` files—the external track’s pub-deletion batch and the silent-channel fix must be
serial).

**New internal documentation constraint**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial;
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial, and 7b’s `Phi` arm must precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “after-the-fact checks,” while
  rules are “before-the-fact judgment.” P9’s scripts cannot prevent “patching when a refactor was
  required”; only the D0–D4 review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative inventory of CI scripts**—the three concurrent inventories
  underlying G3 prevented closure. After this table merges them, the 11 scripts each have one owning
  phase, and report-only status and hardening timing are explicit.
- **P3.5 adopts RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to execute after the
  refactoring”**—its deletion surface overlaps with the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039
  D56). Deferring it until after the refactoring means repeating the same deletions on the new
  grammar, new checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as adopting `2315`/`2341` in 7e
  and adopting RFC-status correction in S4.
- **P5’s steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding the checker split would exceed the rollback granularity.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero caller changes” as its hard acceptance criterion**—the split must be
  independently revertible.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it only says “the fixed defects
  must not be rolled back,” and lacks a requirement to record what was fixed. **Execution
  convention**: every 1.3.x fix’s commit message must reference the fixed test name and defect
  description, as retrospective bisection evidence.
- ~~**7b.1 is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b as two exclusive
  commits under DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 is too coarse**—approximately 89 reference renames; missing one will **silently change
  associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding Level 3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as 7e.1,
  and D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation was merged into 7e.1, with the deletion
  left to P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally assigned to an “independent issue”**~~
  **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: adopted as 7e.2 / 7e.3. The exception table (throw/try) is core language
  semantics and must not be left for future implementation.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into
  P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: assigned to the
  generation-time gate task under P10 S6.

| C1              | `precedence_inline.rs` is revived in P1 and deleted in P8               | **Revive it** (P1’s premise is to revive tests that contain real assertions); P8’s 8.6 deletes the file together with Pratt                                            |
| C2              | “Grammar-driven” commitment vs table-driven implementation              | **Fully implemented**: LALRPOP is adopted; see “Syntax: Complete Grammar-Driven Parsing” in `05`                                                                       |
| C3              | Conflict between the C6 category definition and S1 classification       | **S1 is classified under C6** (revival does not require equivalence criteria, only regression tests); the C6 definition is expanded to “pure deletion or pure revival” |
| C4              | Whitelist for `test_release_plan_spans_consumed`                        | **No whitelist**; the difference set must be empty; if it cannot be empty, the `ReleasePlan` contract is defective → change it to `PlanId` (D20/D41)                   |
| C5              | Unverified internal differences between the two `Aggregation` functions | **P4’s 4.2.7 makes it a mandatory verification item**, to be confirmed line by line during implementation                                                              |
| C6              | The wasm playground fix requires P4’s `ProgramKind`                     | **The wasm-path vulnerability fix is merged into 4.2.8**; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                                |
| C7              | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                      | **Assigned to 04** (P7 batch c), see D21                                                                                                                               |
| C8              | `upvalue_count` correction and the `.42` version number                 | **Fix it + change `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14-16`), see D17                             |
